subject: Re: [AMBER] CUDART lib not found during install

messages.author: Charlotta Lebedenko
messages.body:
Hi Dan,
Sorry for not replying for a while. Thanks so much for your above
suggestions, we tried them both with no luck. We did end up reinstalling
CUDA to get version 11.1 instead of 11.4. We tried using approach #2 that
you suggested, and we are getting the following errors.
Here is the command:
FC=gfortran F77=gfortran F90=gfortran ./configure -noX11 -cuda
--skip-python gnu
Here is the error:
Checking NetCDF...
Using bundled NetCDF library.
Starting NetCDF build.
Configuring NetCDF C interface (may be time-consuming)...
Compiling the NetCDF C interface (may be time-consuming)...
Configuring NetCDF Fortran interface (may be time-consuming)...
Error: NetCDF Fortran configure returned 1
NetCDF configure failed! Check the netcdf_config.log file
in the /mnt/c/Users/banip/amberinstall/amber20_src/AmberTools/src
directory.
Configure failed due to the errors above!
in the log file, we see this error:
configure: finding Fortran compiler
checking whether we are using the GNU Fortran compiler... no
checking whether gfortran accepts -g... yes
checking whether we are using the GNU Fortran 77 compiler... no
checking whether gfortran accepts -g... yes
checking whether Fortran compiler is checked for ISO_C_BINDING support...
yes
checking for Fortran flag to compile .f90 files... unknown
configure: error: Fortran could not compile .f90 files
We cannot figure out this f90 fortran problem.
Please let me know if you have any more suggestions for installing amber on
WSL2.
Best,
Charlotta

>

> instead I think.

> Hope this helps,

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Apr 04, 2022, Charlotta Lebedenko wrote:
>
>configure: finding Fortran compiler
>checking whether we are using the GNU Fortran compiler... no
This is odd. What is the result of "which gfortran" and "gfortan --version"
in your setup?
As a sanity check, try to compile a simple fortran program from the command
line? Does anything look odd?
I think you can find the actual file and compiler invocation in the logs
somewhere. That would show you what netcdf is doing.
Maybe others on the list have seen this problem with WSL2. We have only
limited testing among Amber developers, and certainly have not stumbled
across the problem you are reporting so far.
...regards...dac

> > >

> > > again.
> > >
> > > 2) Although the configure script is soon-to-be-deprecated, it may be
> > > worth a shot. With CUDA_HOME properly set try:
> > >
> > > ./configure -cuda --skip-python gnu
> > > make install
> > >
> > > See if that works. If you only want pmemd.cuda you can do 'make pmemd'
> > > instead I think.
> > >
> > > Hope this helps,
